maria: dropping a quick summary of the perfetto + nvprof dumps from the multi-tenant 2k RPS run. Captured a few 30s windows around the latency spike at T+12m. TL;DR: fused attention variant wins on throughput but we have a persistent KV-cache lookup kernel that's top-2 by GPU time.

maria: raw top-of-trace aggregate (nsys/perfetto):
```
Top kernels by total GPU time (agg over 30s window):
1) fused_attention_fwd_fp16       42.3ms (38%)
2) kv_cache_lookup                28.7ms (25%)
3) cutlass_gemm_fp16              18.1ms (16%)
4) softmax_stable                 10.4ms (9%)
5) layernorm_fwd                  7.9ms (7%)
others: memcpy_htod / kernel_setup / cudaMemset ~6%
```

maria: occupancy / SM util suspects from perfetto counters: fused_attention_fwd shows high SM util (~78%) and good warp efficiency (avg 89%), but kv_cache_lookup has low occupancy (~21%) and extremely poor L2 hit rate (~12%) with DRAM throughput spikes. That smells like memory-bound, divergent access pattern on KV lookup. :thinking:

kevin: can you paste the nvprof / nsight command you used? want to see CTA sizes and whether shared mem bank conflicts show up. also which model/seq-len?

maria: command I used:
```
nsys profile -o run_hit0 --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi \
  --sample=none --duration 30s --timestamps true --force-overwrite \
  --target-processes=all --output-trace=true --activity-regex "CUDA memcpy|kernel" \

nvprof --analysis-metrics -f -o nvprof_out.nvvp --print-gpu-trace ./run_workload.sh
```
Model: 8-layer decoder, seq_len=1024 (mixed batch of 8 and 2), p4d (sm_80), amp fp16.

kevin: thanks. if kv_cache_lookup is low occupancy but high time, check branch-divergence and uncoalesced loads. also see if we have many small kernels i.e. 1 warp per CTA. could be kernel launch overhead from very small work per thread. :eyes:

sam: something I noticed in the timeline — KV lookup spikes line up with cache-miss events on host side when a cold client hits the private cache. On perfetto timeline there's a 1-2ms stall on CPU side followed by a burst of memcpy_htod. So the GPU kernel time includes serialization + wait for host copy in some windows. That could explain the odd L2/DRAM numbers.

olivia: we also saw a perf regression on the canary last week after the batching heuristic change (switched from adaptive-prefetch to static-window 64). Could the batching change cause more fragmented KV lookups (smaller batches per request) and make lookup pattern worse? :thinking:

maria: good call. I compared traces pre/post-heuristic: before the change, kv_cache_lookup had 12ms total time and better L2 hit rate (~48%). after change it's 28ms and lower occupancy. Changed batching reduces prefetch density, so more scatter loads to DRAM.

perf-bot: linked dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/1772003344/flamegraph - contains per-kernel flame + CTA occupancy + L2/DRAM timelines. (private link)

kevin: plan: 1) reproduce with controlled seq_len=1024 single-tenant run to isolate KV behavior, 2) run nsight with `cupti:dram,cache` to capture memory-level stats, 3) experiment with fused vs unfused attention kernels at small batch sizes. I suspect switching to fused_attention_v2 with larger thread-block config might increase L2 reuse.

sam: also try a microbenchmark for KV lookup kernel: synthetic access pattern with same sparsity and batch distribution. If it's memory-bound we can try prefetching into shared memory or change layout to coalesce.

olivia: +1 for synthetic. I'll log an infra job to run a 10-min reproducible trace and tag it with `kv-lookup-investigate`.

maria: follow-up: I'll run nsight with these flags and share the nvprof counters (L2_read_throughput, dram_read_throughput, branch_efficiency, warp_execution_efficiency) and re-run profiler for fused/unfused variants. If KV kernel stays top-2 we should consider kernel rewrite or re-layout of the KV buffers.

maria: action items: run focused nsight (maria), microbenchmark (sam), revert batching heuristic on a canary (olivia) and compare flamegraphs. I'll post TL;DR here when I have the numbers. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: noted. label `perf-investigation/kv-hotspot` added to the run.
